reason: FAQ 5 says account agreements apply only to the individual account used to sign in, organization agreements apply to all accounts in the organization including management and member accounts, and only the management account can accept organization agreements.

The What is AWS Artifact page states on-demand downloads of security and compliance documents, names ISO, PCI and SOC reports as examples, and adds downloads of certifications from accreditation bodies.
The managing agreements page says an account or organization that no longer needs an accepted agreement can terminate it in AWS Artifact and can activate it again later.

The document history row dated December 15, 2025 lists exactly these updates (example IAM policies, AWSArtifactReportsReadOnlyAccess, download instructions) for artifact:ListReportVersions and report versions.

The Aggregators table row gives 50 with 'Can be increased: Yes', and the note says organization and individual account aggregators both count toward that limit; the qualifier correctly records that no account or Region scope is named.

Pricing example 1 (US East, 24 hours, 10 items from each of 100 EC2 instances) states 10 items per resource under continuous, 1 per resource per day under periodic, and the $0.003 and $0.012 per-item prices used in the example.

The retention page says the period is chosen between a minimum of 30 days and a maximum of 7 years (2557 days) and that without a setting ConfigurationItems are stored for the default 7 years (2557 days).

The source data page names CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow logs and GuardDuty findings as the core package, limits GuardDuty findings to enrolled accounts, says optional packages can be started or stopped for a behavior graph at any time, and describes the EKS and Security Hub CSPM packages.

The Detective overview states the pivot from a GuardDuty finding in GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM directly into the Detective console, and the Security Hub CSPM integrations page states that integration needs no additional configuration in either service.
The concepts page defines an attack sequence in these words, and the Extended Threat Detection page says it correlates these events and then generates an attack sequence finding.
The FAQ answer states automated remediation with GuardDuty, EventBridge and Lambda and gives the example of a Lambda function modifying security group rules based on findings.
The foundational data sources page says GuardDuty consumes CloudTrail management events directly from CloudTrail through an independent and duplicated stream of events.
The first sentence of What is Amazon GuardDuty matches the claim word for word.

The Organizations page says the management account can designate any account as delegated GuardDuty administrator and that by default it can enable and manage GuardDuty for all member accounts within that Region.

The history row dated March 30, 2023 announces EKS Runtime Monitoring with the EKS add-on agent collecting runtime events, and the EKS Runtime Monitoring page states the console consolidation and that settings are not migrated automatically.
Under the EventBridge notification frequency heading the page says the frequency for newly generated findings is near real-time and by default cannot be modified.
The export page states 90-day retention of generated findings, export of active findings to EventBridge, and optional export to an S3 bucket to track historical data.

The FAQ answer states independence on first enablement and that automatic agent deployment for Runtime Monitoring could add resource utilization and will create VPC endpoints in the monitored workloads' VPCs.

The FAQ answer to 'Can I write custom detections' says GuardDuty removes the work of maintaining custom rule sets, new detections are continually added, and customer customizations include own threat lists and a trusted IP address list.

The FAQ answer states pay-as-you-go, paying only for usage, and lists the four pricing bases; 'runtime workloads monitored' is a short form of the number and size of EKS or ECS workloads monitored at runtime and adds no new value.

The pricing guide states the per-Region 30-day free trial with some plans enabled automatically, and the table marks Runtime Monitoring, On-demand malware scan, Malware Protection for S3 and Malware Protection for AWS Backup as No under 'Enabled by default'.
The features section lists the foundational data sources as CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs (from EC2 instances) and DNS logs.

The pricing page Malware Protection for S3 section states managed scanning of newly uploaded objects with a finding and EventBridge notification on detection, and the guide says an independently enabled account has no detector ID so no GuardDuty finding is generated.

The 50,000 row and the history dates are supported, but the claim makes 'this default value' the subject of 'can't exceed the number of member accounts in your organization', while the quote says the number of GuardDuty member accounts added through Organizations can't exceed the organization's member count; adjustable true is also not stated.

Footnote 2, linked from the 'Separate free trial availability' header, gives the own 30-day trial for a new plan after the initial trial, and the table marks On-demand malware scan, Malware Protection for S3 and AWS Backup as No in that column.
The FAQ key-benefits answer states GuardDuty is designed to operate completely independently from resources with no performance or availability impact on workloads.
The pricing overview sentence matches the claim word for word.

The RDS Protection page lists Aurora MySQL and PostgreSQL, RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB for login activity, Aurora PostgreSQL and RDS for PostgreSQL for data activity, and says it needs no additional infrastructure and is designed not to affect performance.
The Detector concept says GuardDuty is regional, enabling it in a Region associates the account with a detector ID unique in that Region, and another Region gives a different detector ID.
The Runtime Monitoring page states the OS-level, networking and file events, coverage of EKS, ECS on Fargate and EC2, and that GuardDuty doesn't support EKS clusters running on Fargate.

The SRA Security Tooling page states enablement in all accounts through Organizations, findings handled in the delegated administrator (Security Tooling) account, export of active findings to a central Log Archive bucket to retain them beyond 90 days, and KMS customer managed key encryption.

The Suppression rule concept states attribute-combination suppression, the auto-archive port scan example, that GuardDuty still generates all findings with an immutable history, and that administrator rules apply to members who can't modify them.

The suspend page states no monitoring or new findings, existing findings intact, re-enable later, no charge while suspended, and that protected buckets under Malware Protection for S3 keep their status and keep incurring usage costs.

The findings page says active findings are stored until remediated, findings of deleted, terminated or ineligible resources are deleted after 3 days, and findings closed for any other reason after 30 days.
The quotas row gives a maximum of 500 CIS scan configurations with no quota increase, and the page intro says it lists quotas per AWS Region.

The CIS scans page states benchmarking EC2 operating systems against CIS recommendations, on-demand or scheduled recurring scans targeted by instance tags, the need for EC2 scanning, and lists 'The instance is an Amazon EC2 Systems Manager instance' under instance requirements.
The document history row dated February 12, 2024 says the retention period for closed findings changed from 30 days to 7 days.

Three quotes on two pages state automatic hybrid enrollment with agent-based for SSM-managed and agentless for eligible EBS-backed non-SSM instances, and the scan mode section has the contradicting agent-based default sentence, exactly as the claim reports.
The archived ECR images section says Amazon Inspector does not scan images archived in ECR (imageStatus ARCHIVED).
The scan behaviors section lists the three continuous-scanning triggers (push, relevant new CVE, archived to active) and says on-push repositories are scanned only on push.
